items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Advanced Degree.
Drives motorized equipment: Yes
8 - 13 years of related experience.
Experience engaging advisory boards and volunteer leaders as donors and champions of philanthropic priorities.
Fundraising, institutional advancement, or strategic business development within higher education, academicmedicine, or a similarly complex, multi-layered nonprofit organization.
Minimum of 6 years of experience frontline major-gift fundraising.

Serves as an expert or lead development professional in a specialized area such as major/principal gifts, gift planning or corporate/foundation relations, or a specific academic discipline such as Health Sciences which has an environment that includes, or potentially includes, donors capable of making very significant contributions to the campus and/or medical center. (65% time)

Unit fundraising strategy and program leadership: Serves as senior philanthropic advisor and thought partner to the dean or unit head, translating academic priorities into compelling, fundable initiatives and working with development leadership to set short- and long-range philanthropic strategy. Develops cross-disciplinary "big idea" opportunities and designs the unit's fundraising framework aligned with DAE standards. Owns the unit's fundraising performance and operating rhythm, aligning individual and unit plans with annual expectations and using pipeline and performance data to redirect effort and address risk. Where applicable, provides fundraising leadership to the unit's advisory boards and volunteer leaders, partnering with the dean on board giving expectations, engaging members as donors, and building their focus on and efforts toward growing the philanthropic support of the unit. Directs unit fundraising operations, work allocations, and resources. May oversee the work of volunteers, student workers, or support staff. (20% time)

Development-adjacent integration and execution: Serves as the unit's primary fundraising liaison to Alumni Engagement, Annual Giving, Donor Relations and Stewardship, and central Development partners, aligning engagement and pipeline-building activities with major-gift priorities. Coordinates partners, priorities, timelines, and accountability for fundraising initiatives, so the unit presents one coherent philanthropic strategy to its alumni and donor community. (15% time)
Required to hold valid driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with localpolicies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program.
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Frequently
Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Frequently
Bend: Occasionally
Sit: Frequently
Stand: Frequently
Walk: Frequently
Expert working knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations concepts, principles, procedures, and techniques.
Proven record of personally closing six-figure gifts and leading or partnering on solicitations at the seven-figure or principal gift level.

Expert knowledge of all aspects of the location, including current issues of concern for both the campus and/or throughout higher education/healthcare, generally. Expert knowledge of the location, including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure.
Expert level skills in maintaining confidentiality.
Expert knowledge of applicable laws, rules, regulations, policies, etc.

Expert organizational, analytical and critical thinking skills. Expert project/program management skills, including skills in setting and meeting program/project goals and objectives within budget and time constraints.

Expert written and interpersonal communication skills, including political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships throughout the organization and with outside constituencies. Expert skills in making persuasive and compelling presentations of goals and objectives for a location in order to secure gifts.
Ability to build a donor pipeline, independently plan and manage portfolio activity to meet annual expectations for visits, qualifications, solicitations, and gift production.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively in a matrix, centralized-decentralized development model.
Proficiency with CRM systems (Salesforce preferred) and standard productivity software; maintains timely, accurate data entry of contact reports and prospect plans.
Ability to conceptualize, design, and lead a unit development program, setting strategy and goals in partnership with the dean or unit head.

Working knowledge of charitable gift types and vehicles (outright, pledges, securities, real properties, planned and blended gifts) and of gift agreement, acceptance, and acknowledgement requirements.
